rationale.conceptual: The core method is a standard application of spin-polarized DFT with GGA-PBE to a doped Heusler alloy. The calculation does not involve any novel algorithm or custom theoretical derivation; it relies on well-documented procedures common in computational materials science. While the concept of delocalised magnetism requires careful interpretation, reproducing the numeric results (magnetic moment, band gap) is straightforward with existing DFT codes.
rationale.execution: The reproduction requires a sequence of several DFT stages (supercell construction, geometry optimisation, SCF, non-self-consistent DOS) and subsequent data extraction. Each stage depends on the previous, and the agent must manage input files, job execution, and post-processing correctly. Although the steps are individually standard, the multi-stage pipeline with file-based handoffs and the need to compute derived quantities adds moderate engineering effort.
